extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, IP counsel, in-house counsel, and parties filing or prosecuting patents in China
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how the newly amended Chinese Implementing Rules and Guidelines for Patent Examination affect prosecution strategy in China, including rules for PTA, PTE, design patents, priority restoration, and incorporation by reference for PCT national entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for PTA consideration by the CNIPA, the patent has to be issued i) four years or more after the filing date, AND ii) three years or more after the request of substantive examination. The request for PTA must be made within 30 days of issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA compensates for unreasonable delays due to patent examination by the Chinese Patent Office, provided that the delay is not attributable to the applicant. The PTA concept at CNIPA harmonizes with the general principle of PTA at the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA calculation formula
rubrics_metrics.description: PTA = Date of Issuance – the later of four years from filing and three years from substantive examination – Reasonable Delay – Applicant’s Delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable Delay includes the delay due to reexamination, ownership dispute, or patent application preservation in civil procedures. Applicant’s Delay includes any extensions and the use of deferred examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Extension (PTE) basic entitlement and limit
rubrics_metrics.description: PTE makes up the term of a patent 'pertaining to' a drug marketed in China for regulatory review delay for up to five years, provided that the total patent term with PTE after market approval is no more than 14 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chinese approach to PTE is generally similar to the U.S. For a patent to be PTE eligible, the patent must be directed to a new drug that has not yet been marketed in China or abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTE eligible patent types and exclusivity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Only new drug product patents, preparation method patents, and medical use patents are eligible for PTE. For each new drug, only one patent is eligible for PTE, and for a patent covering multiple new drugs, the patent is eligible for only one of the new drugs covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope of the patent during PTE is limited to the new drug or the approved indications for which PTE is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTE timing and application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a conditional approval of a drug by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA), the calculation is based on the time of conditional approval, but the request for PTE cannot be made until a regular approval by the NMPA. The request for PTE has to be made within three months of the NMPA approval and has to be before the expiration of the eligible patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must track NMPA approval type (conditional vs regular) and ensure PTE requests are timely (within three months of regular approval and before patent expiry) and that the post-approval effective patent term with PTE will not exceed 14 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent subject matter expansion and term
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2020 Patent Law expands eligible subject matter for design patents by introducing partial designs and GUI designs. The term for a design patent is extended to 15 years from the filing date (previously 10 years). Domestic priority for a design patent and international design patents are also made available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider filing design protection for partial aspects of a product and for graphical user interfaces, and take advantage of the longer 15-year term and available priority routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of priority (acceptance and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: CNIPA accepts restoration of the right to priority. A request for restoration has to be made within two months of filing or two months of national entrance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition, addition or correction of a priority claim may be requested within 16 months of the priority date or four months of the filing date. Applicants should act promptly if a priority claim is missed or requires correction to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference for PCT applications upon Chinese national entry
rubrics_metrics.description: CNIPA accepts incorporation by reference as a tool to correct mistakes made to applications filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT). When anything is missing or mistaken in a PCT application, but the priority application has the missing or correct information, incorporation by reference is available to bring anything in the claims, specification, and drawings of the priority application to the PCT application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to requesting incorporation by reference during the international stage, a Chinese translation of the priority application must be provided and a reference to the corresponding disclosure in the priority application must be made upon Chinese national entrance. Use incorporation by reference to fix inconsistencies and align the PCT filing with priority disclosure.
